chunks: And when they unpacked their goods, they found their money returned to them. They said, 'O our father, we have what we sought; our goods have been returned to us. We shall bring grain for our family, keep our brother safe, and add a camel-load's measure; that is an easy measure.'
ai.seo_question: What did Joseph's brothers find when they unpacked their goods in Egypt?
ai.summary: In this verse, the brothers return to Jacob with their goods and money, noting that the Egyptian official (Joseph) not only returned their payment but also invited them to bring their youngest brother to secure a larger measure of grain. This 'extra measure' (kayl ba'ir) serves as a strategic incentive for Jacob to part with Benjamin, highlighting the gradual unfolding of divine plan (tadbeer ilahi) where apparent loss leads to ultimate reunion. The brothers' pragmatic yet slightly naive assessment of the 'small cost' underscores their growing trust in the official's generosity, setting the stage for the deeper trials to come.
